answer: Voting power is capped per identity, so even if an attacker controls thousands of accounts each one can only influence a verdict by a tiny fixed amount, and the total is still limited by how much genuine, recent work the cluster can honestly submit. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. Consider a prism as the anchor of the cost.
